To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding mode of the E isomer is flipped such that it binds in a manner similar to the binding mode of folate, and that the binding mode for the Z isomer is normal, with the furosugar oxygen binding near Glu30.
we have shown that the E isomer of the 5-substituent is preferred for binding in the 4-OH site of folate, while the Z isomer is preferred for binding near the nicotinamide of the cofactor.

the crystal structures of six hDHFR ternary complexes with a series of mixed 2,4-aminopyrimidine isomers and NADPH were determined, the configuration of all of these inhibitors, save one (Z3), was observed as the more active E isomer, and the binding of the Z3 isopropyl analog was observed to be in the normal orientation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, potent inhibitors of human DHFR.
the design of inhibitors of DHFR that are capable of binding to both the human enzyme and the malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum dihydrofolate-reductase.
the design and synthesis of new inhibitors of hDHFR, the enzyme that catalyzes the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E isomer of the furopyridine ring binds preferentially to hDHFR and that the Z isomers bind less favorably.
the E isomers of the compounds studied are more potent inhibitors than their respective Z isomers.

these data show that the Z3 isomer binds to hDHFR in an alternate mode, which is not the same as the E isomers, and the binding of only the Z3 is observed despite the presence of the E isomer in the mixture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have observed a novel binding mode for the furopyrmidine ring, which is flipped such that it is perpendicular to that observed for the resolved 2,4-diarylamino-5-substituted furo[2, 3-d]pyriimidines.
the binding of these isomers is highly selective and the Z isomer is favored over the E isomer in all of the cases examined.
the E isomer is preferred for binding to hDHFR and that a new template can be designed for the Z isomer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding of a single isomer from a mixture of chiral compounds is not uncommon, even though the isomers are structurally related.
it is possible to preferentially select for the E isomer of a chiral inhibitor mixture by crystallization, and that the E isomer is the most potent inhibitor of hDHFR.
the E2 isomer binds to DHFR in the opposite binding mode to that of the Z isomer.
